title: Model ingest: compatibility clarity and acceptance checkpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify the acceptance checkpoints and runtime compatibility signals required for admitting new open model weights into the catalog. Deliver a deterministic checklist that combines static metadata, lightweight runtime probes, and eval-driven behavioral checks so that PM, Eng, and Trust teams have a repeatable admission process and clear rollback triggers.
background:
1) Growing volume of community model submissions has increased variability in runtime behavior (memory, KV cache interaction, quantization sensitivity).
2) Current intake is too handwavy: engineers often triage failures ad hoc and product teams lack reproducible acceptance evidence.
3) We need a small, deterministic set of checks that are fast to run, produce explainable signals, and produce an auto-suggested pin recommendation (hard/soft/unpinned) while preserving human review for high-risk models.
scope_included:
- Define 6 admission checkpoints (metadata, binary compatibility, inference smoke tests, latency/memory profile, targeted evals, security provenance).
- Define threshold values and pass/fail semantics for each checkpoint.
- Produce an 'auto-suggest pin' algorithm that maps signals to one of: hard-pin, soft-pin, or unpinned.
- Implement a one-page PRD and checklist used by intake engineers and PM reviewers.
- Wire acceptance criteria into the intake dashboard for visible pass/fail and actionable diagnostics.
out_of_scope:
- Full implementation of automated gating in production catalog UI (this ticket defines the spec and thresholds only).
- Changes to billing or SLA tiers for pinned models.
- Rewriting runtime kernels or model conversion tooling (separate eng projects).
requirements: REQ-1: Catalog entry must include declared tokenizer and architecture metadata (tokenizer name, vocab size, model family, framework, float vs quant).

REQ-2: Binary compatibility probe: a lightweight runtime loader must be able to initialize the model and run a single forward pass with sequences of length 8 and 512 without OOM or immediate crash on a representative GPU. Failure -> automatic hard-pin recommendation and eng triage.

REQ-3: Latency & memory probe: median p50 token-latency for 32-token sequence and 256-token sequence must be within 2x of a reference model of same family on the same hardware, otherwise recommend soft-pin and annotate reason.

REQ-4: KV cache behavior smoke test: two-step prefix continuation should produce deterministic tokens across repeated runs; divergence > 1 token for top-1 outputs flags a behavioral compatibility risk.

REQ-5: Eval-driven checks: run three small eval suites (safety quick-check, prompt-fidelity, and hallucination heuristics) with predefined thresholds. Any safety regression marks customer_impact as high and requires design/Trust signoff.
REQ-6: Auto-suggest algorithm must output confidence (Low/Medium/High) and recommended pin (hard/soft/unpinned) with an explanation string for each mapping.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: PRD and checklist reviewed and approved by Eng leads (runtime + infra), Trust, and PM. Approval recorded as comments.
AC-2: Prototype probe script exists in repo and runs end-to-end on a test GPU pool producing a report with all six checkpoints for three example community models.
AC-3: Auto-suggest algorithm documented with mapping table and unit tests for mapping logic.
AC-4: Intake dashboard mock shows pass/fail per checkpoint and exposes the explanation string for the pin suggestion. UX mock linked in attachments.
AC-5: Two non-engine reviewers (Trust PM + Security) verified that the security provenance field is mandatory for models that request unpinned release. Evidence attached.
decision_log: 2026-03-04: Adopted hybrid approach: combine static metadata checks with fast runtime probes (target < 15 minutes per model on dev pool).
2026-03-06: Decided auto-suggest remains advisory for P0 models; human sign-off required when customer_impact == high.
2026-03-10: Chose three eval suites (safety quick-check, prompt-fidelity, hallucination heuristics) to balance speed and signal quality.
2026-03-12: Finalized threshold policy for latency (<=2x ref) and KV cache determinism (<=1 token divergence).
open_questions: Q1: Should we require a signed license/provenance doc for all unpinned models, or only for ones that request traffic?
Q2: What is the acceptable false positive rate for the auto-suggest pin algorithm before operators lose trust?
Q3: Do we allow temporary 'ephemeral' catalog entries that expire after 30 days and bypass some checkpoints?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly strict thresholds will bottleneck ingest. Mitigation: allow a soft-pin override path with time-limited canary.
Risk: Probes give inconsistent signals across hardware. Mitigation: run probes on canonical small dev pool and record hardware used in report.
Risk: Teams ignore advisory suggestions. Mitigation: surface explanation strings and require brief justification when overriding recommendations.
